title: Pressure Control Solenoid "H" Control Circuit Low
plain: The computer is watching the pressure control solenoid "H" control circuit and is reading a voltage that is lower than it should be, which often means a short to ground or a failed part. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission sets the fluid pressure that applies the clutches during shifts.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Control wire to the pressure control solenoid "H" shorted to ground
Failed pressure control solenoid "H"
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring in the pressure control solenoid "H" control circuit for rubbed-through insulation touching metal
Check the wiring for a short to ground with a meter
Clear the code and see if it returns right away
fix: Fix any shorted wiring first; if the wiring tests good, replace the pressure control solenoid "H".

title: Pressure Control Solenoid "H" Control Circuit High
plain: The computer is watching the pressure control solenoid "H" control circuit and is reading a voltage that is higher than it should be, which often means a broken ground or a short to power. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission sets the fluid pressure that applies the clutches during shifts.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Control wire to the pressure control solenoid "H" shorted to voltage or the part open inside
Failed pressure control solenoid "H"
Corroded or loose connector
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Inspect the wiring and ground connection for the pressure control solenoid "H" control circuit
Check for wires melted or rubbed together in the harness
Measure the circuit with a meter before replacing parts
fix: Repair the open ground or shorted wire; if the wiring is fine, replace the pressure control solenoid "H".

Harsh, late or erratic shifts

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the pressure control solenoid "J"
Broken or chafed wire in the pressure control solenoid "J" circuit
Failed pressure control solenoid "J"
Blown fuse or failed relay feeding the circuit
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the pressure control solenoid "J", checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and resistance of the part with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the pressure control solenoid "J".

title: Pressure Control Solenoid "J" Performance/Stuck Off
plain: The pressure control solenoid "J" is not responding the way the computer expects. This solenoid inside the automatic transmission sets the fluid pressure that applies the clutches during shifts.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission warning light on
Harsh, late or erratic shifts
Transmission may go into limp mode (stuck in one gear)

causes.name: Sticking pressure control solenoid "J"
Low, dirty or wrong transmission fluid
Worn valve body or internal fluid leak
Worn clutches inside the transmission

checks: Check the transmission fluid level and condition
Look for other transmission codes
Have the solenoid tested and commanded with a scan tool
fix: Service the fluid if it is low or dirty; if the code returns, replace pressure control solenoid "J" or the valve body it sits in.

title: Shift Fork "A" Position Circuit
plain: The computer is watching the shift fork "A" position circuit and has spotted an electrical fault. On dual-clutch and automated manual transmissions, this sensor reports where a shift fork is so the computer knows which gear is engaged.
symptoms: Check engine or transmission light on
Gear changes may fail or be slow
Transmission may not select a gear

causes.name: Unplugged, loose or corroded connector at the shift fork "A" position sensor
Broken or chafed wire in the shift fork "A" position circuit
Failed shift fork "A" position sensor
Missing reference voltage or ground from the computer
Control module fault (rare)

checks: Look over the connector and wiring for the shift fork "A" position circuit, checking for damage, corrosion or a loose fit
Check power, ground and signal with a meter
Clear the code and see if it comes back
fix: Repair the wiring or connector if it is damaged; otherwise replace the shift fork "A" position sensor.
